title: OCX Index Root Config
description: Format-version discovery document served at /config.json. A fixed path convention, not a runtime-discoverable one: a client that understands format_version already knows the full /p/<ns>/<pkg>... path grammar, so there is no packages prefix and no free-text note field (ADR: adr_locked_observation_index_format.md D7).

format_version.description: Monotonically increasing wire-format generation counter. Named format_version, not version, to stay lexically distinct from package-level version concepts.

name_segments.description: Slash-separated segment count a package name must have under this index, counted on the name WITHIN the namespace (the part after ocx.sh/). This deployment serves 2, restating root.schema.json's ^ocx\.sh/<ns>/<pkg>$ as a client-consumable declaration: a client can then know, without asking, that a flat name like ocx.sh/go-task has no root here and resolve it as plain OCI instead of reading the unavoidable 404 as an authoritative refusal. Optional and purely additive — absence means the index declares no constraint and can express every name, which is exactly how a client that predates the field behaves. It is therefore NOT a security control: it only ever narrows what a client asks for, and nothing about yank markers or object-digest verification is delegated to it.
